source.title: Efficient GPT Model Pre-training using Tensor Train Matrix Representation
source.authors: Viktoriia Chekalina; Г. Р. Новиков; Julia Gusak; A. Panchenko; I. Oseledets

record.tranche_reason: The study varies parameter counts in GPT-2-small variants and reports held-out WikiText-103 perplexity, and it compares similar-sized TTM and SVD models. It does not fit scaling laws or use the original scaling-law method.
record.gate_note: The GPT-2-small parameter-count sweep with validation perplexities bears on V1. The similarly sized TTM and SVD comparison bears on V4. The GLUE and summarization results do not test downstream predictability from pretraining loss or scale. Scaling-law statements cited from Kaplan et al. are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: This is a compression-method paper: it trains GPT-2 with Tensor Train Matrix (TTM) layers and compares them with the dense model and an SVD variant. It fits no scaling law and varies no tokens or compute. Its parameter counts change only through TTM rank, a structural change, over less than a factor of 2. Kaplan et al. is cited only to justify one-epoch GLUE fine-tuning. The TTM-vs-SVD gap at matched size is about weight parameterization, not the depth/width shape that V4 names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that TTM layers give a GPT-2 model about 40% lighter, with no significant quality drop on in-domain, out-of-domain and downstream tasks. They also conclude that lower-rank structures such as SVD are less expressive than TTM when trained from scratch under the same conditions.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains GPT-2 variants from scratch using TTM or SVD layer representations and reports perplexity; it does not perform scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The study notes that performance of identical architectures can vary with the training pipeline, but does not test how pipeline choices change the reported scaling relationship.

fits_no_version.finding: At near-equal parameter counts (218M vs 221M), GPT-2 medium with TTM-72 layers reaches out-of-domain WikiText-103 perplexity 30.85, versus 55.46 with SVD-50 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At a fixed parameter count, the factorization of the weight matrices (full-rank TTM vs low-rank SVD) strongly changes language-model loss, unlike depth/width shape.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-2 small with TTM layers at 54–86% of dense size reaches WikiText-103 perplexity 21.33–17.61, versus 17.55 for the dense model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compressed (tensorized) parameterizations can achieve near-dense loss with fewer parameters, so parameter count alone does not fix loss across parameterizations.

record.peer_reviewed: Pacific Asia Conference on Language, Information and Computation
record.problems: The size sweep covers a limited range and reports perplexity rather than fitted cross-entropy scaling laws. The out-of-domain model comparison is limited to the reported models and dataset conditions. The paper reports standard deviation no more than 0.0008 for the five repeated GLUE experiments, but those experiments do not test the claim versions recorded here.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 results for GPT-2 medium, Distil GPT-2 and OPT 350m were not included because their reported training datasets differ, preventing a direct size comparison under matched conditions. Table 6 GLUE and Table 7 summarization results were omitted because they do not report downstream predictability from pretraining loss or scale.

untested.parts: No power-law fit, no token or compute variation, under one order of magnitude in parameters, and size is confounded with layer structure.
Depth and width are never varied at fixed parameter count.
GLUE and summarization are reported for a few models only, with no relation to scale or loss.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V1/V4 labels are removed. The rank sweep compares the authors' own method with the dense baseline over under 2x in parameters. The TTM-vs-SVD gap is a parameterization effect, recorded under fits_no_version. The authors also state that results for identical architectures vary with the training pipeline.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit or exponents; does not vary tokens or compute, cover several orders of magnitude, or establish the non-bottleneck conditions.
Does not vary depth or width; the architecture comparison is between TTM and SVD layer representations, not a wide architectural sweep.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Reference model in a parameter-count sweep; validation perplexity reported.
rows.note: Reference for the GPT-2-small TTM rank variants; this is one point, not a fitted scaling law.
rows.check: Dense reference model for the authors' own compression method, not a scaling-sweep point. A single value cannot bear on a power law.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small TTM-16
rows.operation_detail: TTM rank variant in a parameter-count sweep; validation perplexity reported.
rows.note: Compared with the larger reference model, this smaller variant has higher perplexity.
rows.check: Size changes only through TTM rank, so parameterization is confounded with size. The range is 54–100% (under 2x), so no power-law test is possible. This is the study's own method compared with the dense baseline.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small TTM-32
rows.operation_detail: TTM rank variant in a parameter-count sweep; validation perplexity reported.
rows.note: Compared with the larger reference model, this smaller variant has higher perplexity.
rows.check: Same as r2. Rank-32 has more parameters than rank-16, and perplexity changes only slightly (21.06 vs 21.33). Not a scaling measurement.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small TTM-64
rows.operation_detail: TTM rank variant in a parameter-count sweep; validation perplexity reported.
rows.note: Compared with the larger reference model, this smaller variant has higher perplexity.
rows.check: Same as r2: a TTM-rank variant of the authors' method, not a scaling point.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small TTM-80
rows.operation_detail: TTM rank variant in a parameter-count sweep; validation perplexity reported.
rows.note: Perplexity is close to the larger reference model; this is a narrow parameter range and does not establish a power law.
rows.check: Same as r2: a TTM-rank variant of the authors' method, not a scaling point.

rows.subject: GPT-2 TTM-72
rows.operation_detail: Out-of-domain language-model validation used to compare a TTM layer representation with a similar-sized SVD representation.
rows.note: The authors state the TTM and SVD models were trained from scratch under the same conditions; the parameter counts are similar.
rows.check: Compares the study's TTM method with an SVD factorization at matched parameters. This concerns low-rank versus full-rank weight parameterization, not depth or width shape (V4).

rows.subject: GPT-2 SVD-50
rows.operation_detail: Out-of-domain language-model validation used to compare an SVD layer representation with a similar-sized TTM representation.
rows.note: The authors report this result is worse than TTM-72 despite similar parameter counts and the same stated training conditions.
rows.check: Same as r6. The SVD-50 model is GPT-2 medium with SVD layers, the comparator to the authors' method.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: Perplexity broadly improves with parameter count across this sweep, but the results cover a limited range and do not fit or establish a power law (r1–r5).

reader_labels.label: challenges

reader_labels.reason: The reported perplexities differ substantially between these layer representations at similar parameter counts (r6–r7).
